edges.description: Many missense variants reduce the amount of CNNM2 reaching the plasma membrane.

A CBS-domain substitution abolishes CNNM2-mediated Mg2+ efflux.

edges.description: Less CNNM2 at the plasma membrane means less CNNM2-dependent magnesium transport.

Disturbed neurodevelopment results in intellectual disability.
Speech development is particularly affected.
Fine and gross motor skills are impaired.
Biallelic patients have severe global developmental delay.
Biallelic patients develop microcephaly.

Wide outer cerebrospinal fluid spaces in a biallelic patient, mirrored by cerebrospinal fluid accumulation in the cerebrum of cnnm2b morphant zebrafish.
Neuronal hyperexcitability produces generalized seizures.
Epileptic spasms in one de novo heterozygous infant.
In biallelic patients, refractory neonatal seizures with severe developmental impairment form an epileptic encephalopathy.
Prolonged seizures occur in some biallelic patients.
Patient variants fail to increase cellular magnesium uptake.

nodes.description: The intracellular Bateman module of CNNM2 (residues 429 to 584, two CBS domains) binds ATP in a Mg2+-dependent way, and nucleotide binding switches the CBS module dimer from a twisted to a flat disc-like form that alters the elements linking it to the transmembrane region. The dominant p.Thr568Ile variant, reported in one of the first CNNM2 families, mimics the nucleotide-bound structure and is proposed to lock the module in its flat form. CBS-deleted CNNM2 cannot promote Mg2+ efflux.
nodes.id: Disrupted Mg-ATP Binding by the CBS Module
